sources.title: MQTT Version 3.1.1 — OASIS Standard
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official OASIS standard and inspected its version/status and QoS definitions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: QoS 0 is at-most-once and message loss can occur; QoS 1 can duplicate. These describe protocol message delivery.
sources.applicability: Defines TTS MQTT QoS 0 semantics, not semantic observation delivery or archive idempotency.

sources.title: Webhook Retries — The Things Stack
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current public documentation at access; deployed release unknown.
sources.locator: Availability/default/retry behavior lines 22-37 and retry details lines 40 onward.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official TTS documentation and read feature availability, default behavior, and enabling conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Cloud Plus is required for TTS Cloud. Webhook requests are tried at most once by default; retries require enabling the feature.
sources.applicability: A conditional route only if the chosen deployment supports and enables retries. It does not guarantee exactly-once observations.

sources.title: Storage Integration — The Things Stack
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current public documentation at access; retention is deployment-specific.
sources.locator: How it works, retention, Cloud scope, and batch-delay note, lines 22-34.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official documentation and read retention, stored-message scope, and write timing.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page documents 30-day Cloud retention, 24-hour Sandbox retention, configurable Enterprise retention; Cloud stores uplinks only, and writes are batched with possible delay.
sources.applicability: Can support bounded reconciliation if already enabled; it is not evidence of the club archive or real-time behavior.

sources.title: Troubleshooting Console — The Things Stack

sources.observed_operation: Opened the official troubleshooting page and read the time display and common error passages.

sources.title: LoRaWAN L2 1.0.4 Specification TS001-1.0.4
sources.locator: Section 4.3.1.5, PDF page 22/90, especially rules corresponding to lines 678-789.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official PDF and inspected the frame-counter section, including OTAA reset, ABP persistence, and retransmission rules.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A successful OTAA Join-Accept resets counters; ABP counters must persist through power loss; retransmissions do not increment FCntUp and the Network Server forwards one application-payload instance.
sources.applicability: Applies only if a device uses this LoRaWAN version and behavior. It does not define buffered application sample IDs or prove a device can batch readings.

sources.title: Retrieve Messages — The Things Stack Storage Integration

sources.observed_operation: Opened the public retrieval guide and inspected example envelopes with outer and nested received_at values, gateway rx_metadata time, settings time, f_cnt, and session fields.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Examples show multiple network/gateway receipt timestamps and transport metadata; they do not promise a universal device sample-time field.
sources.applicability: Supports separating transport receipt evidence from observation time; actual payload schema remains a device input.

sources.title: COPY — PostgreSQL 18 documentation
sources.locator: Default COPY error behavior lines 55-57; ON_ERROR semantics lines 145-152; CSV/header/client input sections.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official versioned documentation and searched/read CSV, header, conversion-error, and client-input behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default conversion error behavior is stop; ON_ERROR ignore discards rows. COPY and HEADER MATCH do not provide staff review, dedupe, or correction lineage.
sources.applicability: Supports a proposed PostgreSQL staging/import path only if PostgreSQL 18 is selected.

sources.title: Constraints — PostgreSQL 18 documentation
sources.locator: Unique constraints and NULLS NOT DISTINCT discussion, Section 5.5.3-5.5.4.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official documentation and inspected unique-key and null treatment.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Uniqueness applies to the selected key; by default two nulls are distinct, unless NULLS NOT DISTINCT is chosen.
sources.applicability: A constraint can enforce a known stable sample identity; the documentation cannot supply identity for unknown devices.

sources.title: Transactions — PostgreSQL 18 tutorial
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official tutorial and read its all-or-nothing database transaction description.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A database transaction makes its grouped changes atomic to other transactions; this does not itself coordinate external file storage with database changes.
sources.applicability: Supports only the proposed database-side acceptance workflow, not a validated CSV process.

sources.title: Programming Guide — Apache Beam

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Allowed lateness can let triggers react after a watermark passes a window; lateness is bounded and concerns derived windows, not indefinite raw-event retention.
sources.applicability: Analogy for derived chart refresh only; Beam is not selected as a pilot dependency.

sources.title: TriggerExample.java — Apache Beam source

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: In the example, zero allowed lateness drops a late record; one-day allowed lateness permits late panes. The trigger and bound are example choices.
sources.applicability: A released derived-aggregation example, not a club data-retention policy.

sources.title: Line protocol reference — InfluxDB 3 Core
